name: Mori Kei

influenced_by: a specific early social-networking platform's community features

reacts_against: the loud, maximalist Harajuku street styles (decora, gyaru) that dominated Japanese street-fashion media before it, offering a quiet, muted, nature-focused alternative instead.
article: Mori kei ("forest style") has an unusually specific founding platform: the community coalesced around 2006 on Mixi, a Japanese social networking site that predated most Western platforms' mainstream adoption, where members shared photos of loose, layered, naturalistic clothing in pale, muted tones evoking a quiet, imagined forest life. The style arrived as a deliberate contrast to the louder, more maximalist Harajuku street styles (gyaru, decora) that had dominated Japanese street-fashion media through the preceding years, offering a softer, quieter visual register instead. Mori kei's emphasis on natural fiber, muted color and an unhurried, nature-adjacent mood anticipated several Western internet aesthetics by nearly a decade — cottagecore in particular shares much of its visual logic — though the two developed independently, on different platforms, in different cultural contexts, and direct influence between them is not well documented.

findings: mostly muted — about 65% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
